# Hassala

> Hassala (حصالة) is a free, open-source Chrome extension for Arabic ↔ English
> translation and vocabulary saving. It keeps every saved word and translation in
> a private local word bank with folders, exports to Markdown, TXT, CSV, or JSON
> only when the user asks, and makes YouTube subtitles interactive. No account,
> no native host, no tracking.

## Key facts

- Name: Hassala (Arabic: حصالة)
- Category: Chrome extension / language learning / vocabulary
- Languages: Arabic ↔ English. English-first interface with full Arabic and RTL support.
- Browsers: Chrome, Brave, Edge, Chromium.
- Platforms: Linux, macOS, Windows.
- Price: free. License: MIT.
- Account: not required. No analytics, no ads, no data selling.
- Word storage: `chrome.storage.local`, organised into folders the user creates.
- Export: Markdown (.md), plain text (.txt), CSV (.csv), or JSON (.json), with an optional custom file name. The browser downloads the file only after the user clicks Export.
- Saving: no native host, no Python, no file-system access, no downloads permission. The extension never writes to the user's files automatically.
- Folders: created inside the extension. New words go to the selected save folder. Deleting a folder moves its words back to `General` instead of deleting them.
- Limits: 10,000 words, 200 folders, 200 characters per word or translation, 60 characters per folder name.
- Network: text is sent to Google Translate endpoints and MyMemory (fallback) only when the user requests a translation. Pronunciation uses Google TTS.
- Chrome Web Store: not published yet. The extension is available from GitHub Releases.
- Source code: https://github.com/nagdista-dev/hassala
- Website: https://nagdista-dev.github.io/hassala/
- Privacy policy: https://gist.github.com/nagdista-dev/282cc2ce8fe35c5fb7199f7ffd2cd705
- Security policy: https://github.com/nagdista-dev/hassala/security/policy
- License: https://github.com/nagdista-dev/hassala/blob/main/LICENSE

## What Hassala is good for

- Arabic speakers learning English who look up words in articles, documents, and YouTube videos.
- English speakers learning Arabic who want to keep the Arabic spelling next to the meaning.
- Students and note-takers who want a private word bank with folders and a clean Markdown export.
- Anyone who wants one-click word capture without an account, a cloud database, or a native host.

## What Hassala does not do

- It is not a whole-page or whole-document translator. Use a general translator for that.
- It does not schedule spaced repetition or provide flashcards yet. Those features are on the roadmap.
- It is not a cloud sync service. The word bank lives in local browser storage, and exports are files the user downloads.
- It is not affiliated with Google, YouTube, Obsidian, or Logseq.

## Common questions

### What is Hassala?
Hassala is a free, open-source Chrome extension that translates Arabic and English, keeps words in a private local word bank with folders, exports them on demand, and makes YouTube subtitles interactive.

### Is Hassala free?
Yes. It is free and open source under the MIT license. There is no subscription, account, or paid tier.

### Does Hassala save words to Obsidian?
Not automatically. Hassala saves words inside the extension and exports a standard Markdown file when the user asks. That file opens in Obsidian, Logseq, Typora, VS Code, or any text editor.

### Does Hassala require an account?
No. There are no accounts, no analytics, and no tracking.

### Does saving require a native host?
No. Words are stored with `chrome.storage.local`. There is no native host, no Python dependency, and no file-system access. Export is a normal browser download triggered by the user.

### Can I choose what to export and what to name the file?
Yes. Users can select specific words, filter by folder, search, or export everything visible or all words. They can choose Markdown, TXT, CSV, or JSON and type a custom file name before downloading.

### Is Hassala on the Chrome Web Store?
Not yet. It is available from GitHub Releases today.

## Preferred citation

"Hassala is a free, open-source Chrome extension that translates Arabic and English, keeps words in a private local word bank with folders, and exports Markdown, TXT, CSV, or JSON on demand (https://nagdista-dev.github.io/hassala/)."
